answer: Five auditors are drawn from a rotating pool and score the same submission blind. If any two scores diverge by more than one point, the panel fee splits against the outlier and the divergence report is published with both texts. Buying a verdict means buying four seats of five in a pool that reshuffles every epoch. A canyon opens between the paid grade and the public record, the trellis of past accuracy decides who is drawn again, and a lotus of a submission earns nothing when its reviewers have no history to lose.
